## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Dvādasa akusala* (also referred to as *Dvādasa akusala-cittāni* or *Dvādasa akusalacittuppāda*) is a section of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Catalog; Rhys Davids 1900; Müller 1885]. The text presents an analytical exposition of the twelve unwholesome states of consciousness, classifying them according to whether they are accompanied by gladness, associated with or dissociated from wrong views, and prompted or unprompted [Rhys Davids 1900; Mizuno]. In its opening analysis, it enumerates the psychological constituents—such as contact (*phassa*), feeling, perception, and other causally induced mental states—that arise when an unwholesome thought directed toward sensory or mental objects comes into being [Rhys Davids 1900]. In later analytical condensations of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, these twelve arisings of consciousness are explicitly classified under the Dhamma categories of unwholesome (*akusala*) and base or inferior (*hīna*) [Müller 1885].
